heading: ‘Haven’t applied for patent because want my technique to remain free for all farmers’: Subhash Palekar
name: Subhash Palekar
coverDescription: Subhash Palekar is a celebrated Indian agriculturist known for pioneering the Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF) technique. His innovative approach promotes chemical-free, sustainable farming practices that reduce costs and improve soil health, inspiring farmers across India to embrace eco-friendly agriculture and reconnect with nature.
matter: Subhash Palekar, often called the ‘Father of Zero Budget Natural Farming’ in India, has dedicated his life to revolutionizing the way farmers approach agriculture. Born in Maharashtra, Palekar grew up in a farming family and witnessed firsthand the struggles of rural cultivators who were increasingly dependent on expensive chemical fertilizers and pesticides. Disillusioned by the harmful effects of conventional farming methods, he began a personal quest in the late 1980s to find an approach that was both ecologically sustainable and economically viable for farmers with limited resources.

After years of research and experimentation, Palekar developed Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF) — a holistic method that eliminates the use of chemical inputs entirely. At its core, ZBNF is based on using natural, locally available resources such as cow dung, cow urine, jaggery, and pulse flour to nourish the soil and protect crops. The name ‘Zero Budget’ reflects his belief that farming should be free from the burden of costly loans and external inputs, allowing cultivators to work without falling into debt.

What sets Palekar apart is not just the technique itself but his decision to keep it freely accessible. “I haven’t applied for a patent because I want my technique to remain free for all farmers,” he has often said. In his view, farming knowledge belongs to the community and should not be monetized at the expense of those who depend on it for survival. This open-access philosophy has enabled thousands of farmers across India to adopt ZBNF without barriers, creating a grassroots movement toward chemical-free agriculture.

ZBNF goes beyond just replacing synthetic inputs — it transforms the relationship between farmers and their land. Palekar’s teachings emphasize working with nature rather than against it, fostering biodiversity, improving water retention, and revitalizing soil health. By relying on natural processes, ZBNF farmers often report healthier crops, improved yields over time, and resilience against droughts and pests. The method also reduces greenhouse gas emissions, aligning with global calls for climate-friendly agricultural practices.

Over the decades, Palekar has traveled extensively, conducting thousands of workshops, training programs, and farmer rallies. His sessions are not just technical tutorials but motivational gatherings, where he encourages cultivators to regain confidence in their traditional wisdom and reclaim their independence from agribusiness corporations. Many farmers who once struggled under debt have found renewed hope and financial stability through adopting ZBNF, often becoming advocates for the method within their own communities.

His influence has reached policy circles as well. Several Indian states, including Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Himachal Pradesh, have integrated ZBNF into their agricultural policies, providing training and support to scale up adoption. Palekar’s work has also drawn international attention, with agricultural scientists, environmentalists, and policymakers studying its potential as a sustainable farming model for developing nations. Despite the accolades and awards he has received, Palekar remains deeply rooted in his mission, prioritizing the welfare of farmers over personal recognition.

He has also authored several books and manuals on natural farming, which have been translated into multiple Indian languages. These works serve as comprehensive guides for farmers, detailing everything from soil preparation to pest management, and offering insights on how to transition from chemical-dependent methods to natural farming without financial strain.

Palekar’s vision also involves protecting indigenous cow breeds, which are integral to the ZBNF system. He advocates for preserving these breeds not only for their agricultural utility but also for their cultural significance in rural India. His approach intertwines environmental sustainability with the preservation of traditional farming knowledge that has been passed down for generations.

Looking ahead, Palekar envisions a future where every farmer in India embraces natural farming, leading to healthier food, cleaner water, and restored ecosystems. He believes that true prosperity lies not in industrial growth alone but in the harmonious coexistence of human activity and nature. For him, Zero Budget Natural Farming is more than a technique — it is a movement of liberation, dignity, and ecological balance that has the power to reshape the future of agriculture for generations to come.

heading: Meet Madhavi, a plant mom and beginner’s guide to terrace gardening
name: Mad Gardener Madhavi
coverDescription: Mad Gardener Madhavi is a captivating story about a passionate gardener whose love for plants goes beyond the ordinary. Madhavi’s unconventional methods and boundless enthusiasm inspire readers to embrace creativity and patience in gardening, showing how nature and madness can beautifully coexist to create thriving green spaces.
matter: For most people in Andhra Pradesh, that “beginner’s guide to gardening” was Madhavi Guttikonda, a caring plant mom, who has carved her own niche in organic terrace gardening. From sowing flower seeds in her small space a decade ago to nurturing a 1,800 sq ft garden with an ever-expanding variety of organic produce and winning Rythu Nestham Award in the terrace gardening category for the year 2021, this Vizagite’s gardening journey has been fruitful not only to her but also to the audience of her YouTube channel, ‘Mad Gardener’, on which she shares the knowledge she has acquired through observation, experience and experiments in terrace gardening.

Speaking to TNIE, Madhavi Guttikonda, the 43-year-old terrace gardener from Visakhapatnam said, “For me, the word peace is synonymous with gardening. Initially, being an anthophile (someone who loves flowers), I started with a few flowering plants like roses, hibiscus, fragrant flowers, and some seasonal flowers. But it was when I moved to my own house that my idea of greens started taking shape. I switched to complete organic terrace gardening and started with growing leafy vegetables.”

Needless to say, they had to be some of the most delicious vegetables I had ever eaten,” Madhavi beamed. “Instead of merely reaping the benefits all the time, we get to add and tend to nature through gardening while also reducing our ecological footprint,” she noted.

Half a decade ago, she took up growing veggies like tomatoes, radish, aubergines, carrot, sweet potatoes, different varieties of beans, cabbage, cauliflower, lettuce, almost all types of gourds, and medicinal plants. She also nurtures mushroom, turmeric plants and fruits like guava, dragon fruit, papaya, mulberries, cherries, sweet lime, lemon, banana, sugarcane, etc.

I keep on experimenting with seasonal and exotic varieties. Experiments did fail sometimes, but it never deterred me from trying,” said the gardener. “It feels rewarding every time I take a stroll in my terrace garden. Besides physical health, gardening greatly benefits mental and emotional well-being as it soothes our senses and helps us stay connected to nature,” Madhavi said.

Stating that the yield from her garden alone takes care of a significant portion of her family’s food needs round the year, Madhavi observed,  “Being able to harvest for ourselves and our family in a time of crisis, be it a virus outbreak or exorbitant prices, feels so satisfying.”

On the suggestion of her children, the plant mom took her baby steps on YouTube in 2018 by starting her channel ‘Mad Gardener’. The channel now has 4,83,000 subscribers. Not just that, this bona fide gardener also has a notable presence on Instagram with 45,000 followers and 2,18,000 on Facebook.

Her social media journey has become more than just gardening tutorials. She actively engages with her audience, answering questions, giving personalized tips, and even addressing common plant problems such as pest control, soil enrichment, and seasonal care routines. Many of her viewers have shared before-and-after pictures of their gardens, crediting her for inspiring them to start their own green spaces.

Madhavi also participates in community gardening initiatives, helping local schools, housing societies, and NGOs set up terrace gardens. These projects are aimed not only at producing fresh food but also at educating younger generations about sustainability and the joy of growing one’s own food. She often says that even a single plant grown at home is a step toward a healthier planet.

Her ultimate dream is to see every household in urban India growing at least some of its own vegetables and herbs, thereby reducing dependence on chemically grown market produce. For her, terrace gardening is not just a hobby but a movement—one that blends beauty, sustainability, and self-reliance into a single act of nurturing nature.

heading: Charles Dowding: Champion of the No-Dig Gardening Revolution
name: Charles Dowding
coverDescription: Charles Dowding is a renowned British gardener and pioneer of the no-dig gardening method. His sustainable techniques emphasize soil health, reduced labor, and increased yields by avoiding soil disturbance, inspiring gardeners worldwide to adopt eco-friendly and productive growing practices.
matter: Charles Dowding is a celebrated British horticulturist best known for popularizing the no-dig gardening method—a technique that has transformed the way thousands of gardeners think about soil management and crop production. With decades of hands-on experience, Dowding has demonstrated that minimal soil disturbance leads to healthier ecosystems, higher yields, and reduced weed problems.

The core principle of no-dig gardening is simple yet powerful: allow the soil structure to remain intact, preserving its natural layers and the beneficial organisms within it. Instead of tilling or digging, organic matter such as compost is applied to the surface, where it slowly integrates into the soil through natural processes like worm activity and microbial action.

Dowding began experimenting with no-dig techniques in the early 1980s, initially facing skepticism from traditional growers who believed that digging was essential for aeration and fertility. Over time, his meticulous trials proved that undisturbed soil not only retains more moisture and nutrients but also fosters a vibrant soil food web, resulting in vigorous, pest-resistant plants.

At his farm, Homeacres in Somerset, England, Dowding conducts side-by-side trials comparing dig and no-dig plots. The results consistently show that no-dig beds produce equal or greater harvests with far less labor, while maintaining better soil structure and fewer weeds over time. These trials have become a cornerstone of his educational outreach, providing concrete evidence to back his approach.

In addition to his practical work, Dowding has authored multiple books and guides that have become essential reading for both beginner and experienced gardeners. Titles like 'No Dig Organic Home & Garden' and 'Skills for Growing' combine step-by-step techniques with seasonal tips, making the no-dig method accessible to a global audience.

Through his popular YouTube channel, with millions of views, Dowding shares tutorials, garden tours, and seasonal updates. His calm, methodical style and clear explanations have made him a trusted mentor to gardeners worldwide. Viewers appreciate his willingness to share both successes and challenges, making his advice grounded and relatable.

Beyond digital media, Dowding offers in-person workshops at Homeacres and speaks at gardening events around the world. His sessions blend scientific insight with practical demonstrations, showing that sustainable gardening is achievable in spaces ranging from large allotments to small urban balconies.

Environmental sustainability is at the heart of his work. By reducing soil disturbance, the no-dig method helps sequester carbon, improves water retention, and supports biodiversity. In an era of climate change and soil degradation, Dowding’s approach offers a path forward for both home gardeners and commercial growers seeking resilience and efficiency.

Dowding also addresses common myths, such as the belief that composting is overly complicated or that weeds cannot be controlled without digging. His real-world examples show how mulch, cover crops, and timing can dramatically reduce weed growth while enhancing soil fertility naturally.

Looking ahead, Charles Dowding envisions a future where no-dig gardening becomes the default practice, empowering people to grow food more efficiently while healing the planet’s soils. His work continues to inspire a global community of gardeners who see themselves not just as food producers but as stewards of the earth.

heading: Huw Richards: Inspiring the Next Generation of Sustainable Gardeners
name: Huw Richards
coverDescription: Huw Richards is a passionate horticulturist, author, and environmental advocate whose innovative work in sustainable gardening and permaculture has inspired a global audience. Through his engaging content, practical tips, and infectious enthusiasm, Huw empowers gardeners of all ages to grow their own food in eco-friendly and rewarding ways.
matter: Huw Richards is one of the most recognizable young voices in the world of gardening and sustainable food production. Known for his dedication to permaculture principles and his approachable teaching style, he has inspired millions of people to grow their own food, regardless of their experience level or available space.

His gardening journey began in childhood, nurtured by his family’s love for homegrown produce. One of his earliest and fondest memories comes from primary school, when his father encouraged him to soak beetroot seeds in warm water before planting. That moment sparked a lifelong passion for growing, and it wasn’t long before he began experimenting with different crops.

At the age of ten, Huw developed a particular fondness for redcurrants, which he found to be both delicious and surprisingly productive, even in shadier parts of the garden. He began propagating and selling soft fruits, laying the groundwork for his understanding of horticulture and small-scale enterprise.

By the age of twelve, Huw had launched his YouTube channel, aiming to share his experiments, successes, and failures with a wider audience. His videos quickly gained popularity thanks to his clear explanations, youthful energy, and willingness to show the realities of gardening—not just the picture-perfect moments.

After completing his A-levels, Huw decided to commit fully to his gardening career, making content creation, writing, and public speaking his full-time focus. Today, his YouTube channel boasts hundreds of videos on topics ranging from composting and seed saving to designing efficient vegetable beds and integrating permaculture systems.

Huw’s work is deeply influenced by fellow sustainable growers, including Charles Dowding, whose no-dig market garden remains one of Huw’s favorite examples of productive and environmentally friendly food production. He also admires horticulturist James Wong, whose efforts to introduce new and exciting edible plants to British gardens align with Huw’s own desire to diversify homegrown food sources.

While he enjoys growing a wide variety of crops, Huw has a soft spot for overlooked vegetables like the humble swede. In his eyes, swedes are an underappreciated gem—hardy, nutritious, and perfect for the British climate, offering a low-calorie alternative to mashed potatoes.

One of the guiding principles in Huw’s gardening philosophy is the rejection of perfectionism. He believes that striving for flawlessness in the garden can be counterproductive, leading to wasted time and missed opportunities. Instead, he encourages gardeners to embrace imperfection, learn from failures, and celebrate successes, however small they may be.

Huw is also a strong advocate for making gardening accessible to everyone, regardless of budget. Many of his videos focus on cost-saving techniques, such as building raised beds from reclaimed materials, making homemade compost, and starting seeds in upcycled containers.

In addition to his online work, Huw is an author of several gardening books aimed at helping beginners and seasoned gardeners alike. His writing combines practical step-by-step guides with personal anecdotes, making the process of growing food feel approachable and enjoyable.

Beyond the technical aspects of gardening, Huw’s message is rooted in community, resilience, and a deeper connection to nature. He believes that gardening is not only a way to feed oneself but also a way to improve mental health, strengthen local food systems, and take meaningful action against climate change.
From small balcony planters to large-scale vegetable plots, Huw’s teachings prove that anyone can grow their own food and play a part in creating a greener, healthier future.

heading: Mark Valencia: Growing a Self-Sufficient Life
name: Mark Valencia
coverDescription: Mark Valencia is a respected Australian gardener, writer, and advocate for self-sufficiency. Through his platform 'Self Sufficient Me', he shares practical advice, inspiring stories, and hands-on gardening knowledge, encouraging people to grow their own food, live sustainably, and reconnect with nature.
matter: Mark Valencia has become a leading voice in the self-sufficiency movement, blending his passion for gardening with his dedication to sustainable living. A former Australian Army serviceman who retired after 21 years, Mark now devotes his life to inspiring others to take control of their food, health, and lifestyle through practical, achievable steps.

His platform, 'Self Sufficient Me', is both a personal journey and a thriving community hub for like-minded individuals around the world. The name reflects his belief that self-sufficiency is not about isolation, but about empowerment—learning to do more for ourselves while also sharing knowledge and experiences with others.

Mark's mission is symbolized in the logo of 'Self Sufficient Me'—an eye with the Earth as its pupil, representing a vision of learning from nature rather than working against it. He warns of the dangers of over-reliance on chemicals and industrial shortcuts, emphasizing that indiscriminate pesticide use destroys the natural balance that allows ecosystems to thrive.

By observing and respecting nature’s balance, Mark believes we can create our own backyard micro-ecosystems where plants, animals, and humans coexist in harmony. He promotes practices like companion planting, organic pest control, composting, and soil regeneration, not just as techniques but as philosophies for a healthier planet.

For Mark, self-sufficiency goes beyond growing food—it’s a mindset. He sees it as a way of life that encourages people to learn new skills, reuse and recycle, reduce waste, and take personal responsibility for their impact on the environment. It’s about being resourceful, resilient, and proactive rather than outsourcing every aspect of our lives.

Through his YouTube channel, blog, and social media presence, Mark teaches viewers how to grow fruit and vegetables, raise chickens, preserve food, and integrate these activities into a fulfilling lifestyle. His approachable, down-to-earth style makes even complex gardening techniques feel accessible to beginners while still offering valuable insights to experienced growers.

Mark’s philosophy is grounded in the idea that self-sufficiency is not about perfection or total independence. Instead, it’s about taking steps—big or small—toward a healthier, more sustainable way of living. Whether that means growing a few herbs in a balcony planter or transforming an entire backyard into a food forest, every effort counts.

He often reminds his audience that the rewards of self-sufficiency are not only practical but deeply personal. The joy of harvesting your own produce, the satisfaction of creating something with your own hands, and the peace that comes from a closer relationship with nature are benefits that money can’t buy.

Mark also emphasizes the community aspect of self-sufficiency. By sharing successes, failures, and lessons learned, we not only grow better gardens but also grow stronger connections with one another. In a world increasingly disconnected from the sources of our food, his message is a timely reminder that we all have the power to make a change—starting in our own backyards.

With humor, humility, and a genuine love for the land, Mark Valencia continues to motivate people across the globe to 'look, and see the Earth'—to understand it, respect it, and work with it. His journey proves that self-sufficiency is not a destination, but a rewarding, lifelong adventure.
